newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO defence ministers meet eastern Europeans.
newsitem.headline: NATO defence ministers meet eastern Europeans.

text.p: NATO defence ministers met their colleagues from eastern Europe on Friday, a day after the United States said a first enlargement of the alliance behind the former Iron Curtain should be limited to three nations.

The meeting, which includes countries taking part in the alliance's Partnership for Peace programme, was the first with Slovenia and Romania since Washington on Thursday poured cold water on their hopes of being among the first ex-communist states to join the alliance.

Washington caught its NATO allies off guard during the two-day meeting of defence ministers from the western military alliance with its announcement that only Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic should be in NATO's first wave of expansion.
Although Washington's decision is expected to be decisive, some of its European allies have vowed to fight on, at the alliance's July 8-9 summit in Madrid, for Slovenia and Romania to be invited in.
France and the supporters of a broader expansion argue that the two countries need to be included in order to maintain a balance between NATO's northern and southern flanks
